title: TE James Thornton v. Westminster Presbytery (Cases 2003-02 and 2003-05)
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the challenge to the investigation of TE Frank Smith’s secret recording and remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation. It rejected claims concerning the investigation of alleged lying and threats, partiality, and an unbiblical secret-recording policy. The voluntary-prosecutor issue was moot because TE Roberts declined the invitation.
first_summary: Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s investigation and decision not to institute process against TE Frank Smith over a secretly recorded telephone call and related allegations. The SJC required a new BCO 31-2 investigation because Presbytery had not timely obtained the other participant’s testimony or examined relevant legal and confessional questions. It rejected claims concerning alleged lying and threats, partiality, and an unbiblical policy, and remanded the recording matter to Presbytery.
summary: Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s investigation of TE Frank Smith’s secret recording and its refusal to institute process. The SJC remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation because Presbytery had not timely obtained the other participant’s testimony or examined relevant legal and confessional questions. It rejected claims concerning alleged lying and threats, partiality, and an unbiblical recording policy. The invitation of an outside voluntary prosecutor was moot because he declined; only a separate concurrence found the invitation improper.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The heading identifies the joined complaints as Cases 2003-2 and 2003-5, Thornton v. Westminster Presbytery; the judgment was adopted 18–1 (lines 13, 157–159; printed pp. 99, 104).
evidence_notes.dispute: The four issues concern the secret-recording investigation, alleged lying and threats, asserted partiality, and the biblical validity of Presbytery’s policy (lines 65, 71–80; printed p. 101).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Issue 1 was sustained and remanded for a new investigation; Issues 2–4 were rejected. The majority identified omitted testimony and unresolved legal and confessional questions (lines 81–145; printed pp. 101–104).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The prosecutor invitation was held moot; later evidence could permit future process. A concurrence deemed the invitation improper, while the dissent disputed the mandated investigative steps (lines 111–151, 161–237; printed pp. 102–107).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference.
